Title: Adobe Commerce/Magento Improper Input Validation Remote Code Execution
Description: The public storefront runs an unpatched Adobe Commerce/Magento build vulnerable to the 'Cosmic Sting' checkout flow input validation flaw, allowing template/OS command injection during order placement.
Consequence: Unauthenticated remote code execution as the web service account, giving an attacker a foothold inside the DMZ.
Remediation: Apply the Adobe Commerce/Magento security patch (2.4.3-p2/2.4.4-p2 or later); enable a WAF rule set covering the checkout flow; run periodic CMS vulnerability scanning.

Title: Webshell Upload via Unrestricted Media Upload Endpoint
Description: Once a foothold is established, the storefront's media/import endpoint accepts .php files disguised with double extensions, allowing webshell placement.
Consequence: Full remote code execution on the DMZ web server usable as a pivot point into internal networks.
Remediation: Enforce server-side MIME/type validation and extension allow-listing; store uploads outside the web root; disable PHP execution in the uploads directory.

Title: Firewall ACL Permits DMZ-to-Corporate-LAN Traffic on All Ports (Excessive Firewall Rule)
Description: The firewall rule between the DMZ (VLAN 20) and the Corporate LAN (VLAN 10) is defined as 'DMZ-net ANY -> Corp-net ANY ALLOW' instead of restricting to the specific helpdesk ticket-sync port (8080) needed.
Consequence: A foothold on any DMZ host can reach any port/service on any Corporate LAN host, drastically expanding the pivot surface beyond the intended helpdesk-only channel.
Remediation: Rewrite the firewall policy to allow only the specific helpdesk-sync tuple; deny-all as default; document rule owners and review quarterly.

Title: Local Administrator Password Reuse Across Workstations and File Server
Description: The same local Administrator account password is used across FILESRV01, WKS-ACCT01, and WKS-SUPPORT01, discoverable via credential dumping after initial foothold.
Consequence: Compromise of a single workstation credential allows pass-the-hash lateral movement to all machines sharing the password.
Remediation: Deploy Microsoft LAPS to randomize and rotate local admin passwords per host; audit for shared local accounts.

Title: Plaintext Service Account Credentials in Backup Script on File Share
Description: A scheduled-task backup script stored on the '\\FILESRV01\IT-Scripts' share contains the 'svc_backup' account username and password in plaintext, left over from initial Veeam job configuration.
Consequence: Any user who can reach the file share (directly or via lateral movement from a compromised workstation) can read the svc_backup credential; the same account is also valid as local Administrator on PAY-ADMIN01, so this leak hands over administrative access to the payment zone with no further exploitation needed.
Remediation: Remove plaintext credentials from scripts; use Veeam's credential manager / a secrets vault with runtime injection; restrict the IT-Scripts share to the IT-Admins group only.

Title: Weak Non-Rotated Password on Backup Service Account ('svc_backup')
Description: The 'svc_backup' domain account, used by BACKUP-MGR01 to run scheduled Veeam jobs, has a weak password that has not been rotated since initial deployment.
Consequence: A cracked or recovered svc_backup credential can be reused wherever the account has been granted access.
Remediation: Rotate to a 25+ character randomly generated password or migrate to a Group Managed Service Account; enable auditing on the account's authentication events.

Title: Backup Management Console Uses Default Installation Credentials
Description: The Veeam Backup & Replication console is still configured with the default installation service account password.
Consequence: Access to backup infrastructure allows an attacker to browse/restore backup archives or tamper with backup jobs.
Remediation: Change all default credentials immediately post-install as part of the hardening checklist; restrict console access with a jump-host requirement.

Title: Backup Agent Account Granted Local Administrator on Payment-Zone Jump Host (Excessive Privilege)
Description: The 'svc_backup' account, which authenticates from the Corporate LAN backup manager per RULE-EL-009, has been granted local Administrator rights on PAY-ADMIN01 rather than a scoped backup-operator role.
Consequence: Any actor in possession of the svc_backup credential is granted full administrative control of a host inside the PCI CDE, not merely file-level backup access — collapsing the segmentation boundary the backup exception was meant to preserve.
Remediation: Recreate the backup agent identity with the Veeam-specific least-privilege backup operator role; do not reuse a general-purpose domain service account for cross-zone backup jobs; require a dedicated non-domain credential for any CDE-facing service.

Title: Payment Zone Backup Path Crosses PCI Segmentation Boundary (Compliance Gap)
Description: Segmentation testing shows the PCI CDE (VLAN 30) is reachable from the Corporate LAN via the backup agent channel (RULE-EL-009), a path present in the network diagram but not scoped down to a dedicated backup network or jump host as PCI DSS segmentation testing guidance recommends.
Consequence: The backup exception is a documented but under-controlled pathway into the CDE; combined with credential-hygiene issues on the account it depends on, it represents a realistic route into cardholder data systems and a likely QSA finding.
Remediation: Terminate backup jobs into the CDE via a dedicated, tightly scoped jump host with MFA and session recording rather than a directly-addressable agent account; re-test segmentation before the next PCI assessment cycle.

Title: Oracle Database Cardholder Data Stored Without Column-Level Encryption
Description: The 'CARDHOLDER_TXN' table stores primary account numbers (PANs) in cleartext columns rather than using column-level encryption or tokenization, relying solely on network isolation for protection.
Consequence: Any authenticated access to the database yields cleartext cardholder data directly.
Remediation: Implement column-level encryption or tokenization for PAN fields via the HSM-GW01 key management service; restrict DB-level access to the payment switch service account only.

Title: Payment Switch Software Missing Vendor Security Update
Description: PAY-PROC01 runs a payment switch application built on an outdated Craft CMS component bundled with a third-party reporting dashboard, missing a vendor-issued patch for a remote code execution flaw in that component.
Consequence: If network access to the CDE is obtained, this unpatched component allows remote code execution on the payment switch itself.
Remediation: Apply the vendor's security update for the bundled reporting dashboard; remove the component entirely if the reporting feature is unused; restrict management-plane access to PAY-ADMIN01 only.

Title: HSM Gateway Firmware Below Vendor-Supported Baseline
Description: HSM-GW01 is running a firmware revision two major versions behind the vendor-supported baseline, missing hardening improvements to the key-ceremony API.
Consequence: Reduces defense-in-depth around key management operations should an attacker already have CDE network access.
Remediation: Schedule a maintenance window to apply the latest vendor firmware and re-validate FIPS 140-2 compliance post-upgrade.

Title: Fortinet FortiOS SSL-VPN Authentication Bypass
Description: The SSL-VPN portal runs an unpatched FortiOS build vulnerable to an authentication bypass via a crafted HTTP request, allowing an attacker to add arbitrary SSH keys or read admin credentials without authenticating.
Consequence: Attacker obtains administrative access to the VPN gateway without any valid credentials.
Remediation: Upgrade FortiOS to a fixed release (7.2.2/7.0.7/6.4.11/6.0.14 or later); force password reset for all VPN and local admin accounts post-patch; enable MFA on the SSL-VPN portal.

Title: Zerologon - Netlogon Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Description: DC01 is missing the August 2020 security update, leaving the Netlogon Remote Protocol vulnerable to an authentication bypass that allows resetting the Domain Controller's own machine account password.
Consequence: Trivial unauthenticated Domain Admin compromise; from here the attacker owns the entire Active Directory forest.
Remediation: Apply the August 2020 Windows Server cumulative update immediately; enable enforcement mode for Netlogon secure channel; monitor Event ID 5829.

Title: Azure Blob Container Publicly Readable - Contains Customer Export File
Description: The blob container 'elihowa-product-images', intended for public product photos, has anonymous read access enabled at the container level and contains an accidentally-uploaded 'customer_export_2025Q1.csv' with names and email addresses.
Consequence: Anyone on the internet can enumerate and download the container contents, harvesting customer PII (GDPR-relevant exposure).
Remediation: Disable anonymous container access; move the export file to a private container with SAS-token access; enable Azure Storage lifecycle scanning for misplaced sensitive files.

Title: Order API Uses Hardcoded JWT Signing Secret
Description: The Order Processing API's JWT signing secret is a hardcoded string in the application's source repository rather than a securely generated, environment-injected value.
Consequence: An attacker with source or config access can forge valid session tokens for any customer account.
Remediation: Migrate the signing secret to a vault-managed value generated with sufficient entropy; rotate the current secret; add secret-scanning to the CI/CD pipeline.

Title: Vulnerable Dependency in Order API (ReDoS via minimatch)
Description: The Order Processing API bundles an outdated 'minimatch' npm package vulnerable to a regular-expression denial-of-service on crafted input strings.
Consequence: An attacker can degrade API availability with a small number of crafted requests.
Remediation: Upgrade the 'minimatch' dependency to >=3.0.5 / 5.1.2; run 'npm audit' as part of the CI pipeline going forward.

Title: Remote Support Tool Enabled Without MFA on Support Workstation
Description: WKS-SUPPORT01 has a remote-support agent (used for customer troubleshooting sessions) configured to accept connections with password-only authentication, no MFA.
Consequence: A phished or reused credential grants an attacker interactive remote access to the workstation without any secondary factor.
Remediation: Enforce MFA on the remote support tool's authentication policy; restrict which accounts may initiate inbound remote sessions.

Title: Network Print Appliance Running End-of-Life Firmware
Description: PRINT01 is running vendor firmware that reached end-of-life two years ago and no longer receives security updates.
Consequence: Limited direct impact; primarily a footprint/attack-surface concern and a compliance finding for asset lifecycle management.
Remediation: Replace or upgrade the print appliance to a currently-supported firmware line; segment print services onto a dedicated low-trust VLAN.

Title: Load Balancer TLS Configuration Permits Deprecated Cipher Suites
Description: LB01's TLS configuration still permits TLS 1.0/1.1 and several deprecated cipher suites for backward compatibility with legacy partner integrations.
Consequence: Increases susceptibility to downgrade and cipher-suite exploitation attacks against traffic to the storefront.
Remediation: Disable TLS 1.0/1.1 and deprecated ciphers; require TLS 1.2+ with modern AEAD cipher suites only; coordinate the legacy partner cutover date.
